contract.purpose: Machine-readable ledger of measured facts. Read this instead of re-deriving state from prose; query with scripts/context.py evidence [--topic T] [--all].

status_values.superseded: replaced by a later measurement; see superseded_by
status_values.historical: true at the time on an old baseline; do not use as current state

contract.rule: When a new measurement replaces an entry, set status=superseded and superseded_by, and add the new entry. Never silently edit values.

Evaluation splits are machine-enforced via manifest 'split': development = b000-k20/k40, b001-k20 (+new trajectories b000-k15, b001-k30); validation = b000-k10; final_holdout = b001-k40 (both runs; provisional-v1 contamination noted) and b001-k10. final_holdout is skipped by every analysis tool unless --open-final-holdout.

First Stage A run: descriptors worsened LOSO prediction of placed-to-go and correlated inversely, caused by settled-only enumeration (endgame runs on release candidates) and deterministic-scan attempt budgets producing false zeros.

Stride systematic sampling calibrates: release series exact at stride<=16 and stable, settled series sparse (~2-20% error from stride 16, presence detection limited), combined simultaneous bound identical between stride 16 and 4. The former false-zero snapshot truly has 0 settled anchors but ~4.8k release anchors with combined bound 7 vs actual placed-to-go 5.

On the pre-trunk baseline (main d3986a9), floor-resting candidates were rejected by the inclusion check for lack of a floor lift, causing candidate starvation and blind-fallback transport collisions; fixed by FLOOR_ACTION_LIFT and vectorized generation. Superseded as a diagnosis of current behaviour by the release settle-topple evidence.

With the calibrated instrument (stride 16, converged, no cap firing), V_cap(s) descriptors do not explain placed-to-go beyond step/volume/case/pool (LOSO MAE 0.979 -> 1.456 when added; all residual Spearman |rho|<=0.24). Mechanistic byproduct: release acceptance capacity for the largest class persists to terminal steps (cap_volume ~constant, thousands of anchors) and settled-zero states still placed 5 more items -- episodes end by physics failure (release topple), not capacity exhaustion, on these 24 snapshots. Stage B, if pursued, must not use placed-to-go as its label; priority stays with the rotation-risk line.

Mechanical topple features (support-polygon edge margins, critical angle, energy barrier, drop-energy ratio; MATHEMATICAL_MODEL 5.2.1, predicted-contact-state inputs only) dominate the static Phi on every frozen-protocol metric for rotation: LOSO AUC 0.841 [0.776,0.898] vs 0.732 [0.646,0.807]; worst-direction extrapolation 0.771 vs 0.638; within-snapshot discordant-pair ranking accuracy 0.842 vs 0.720 (n=4884 pairs). Single feature log1p(eta) alone (0.825) beats the full static combination. Adding static to mechanics slightly hurts rotation (0.827) but helps not_placed_safe (0.838 vs 0.821). Coefficients remain unfrozen; feature-set choice among {static, mech, static+mech} goes to the validation split per protocol.

Offline rule-family comparison on held-out mechanics P_hat (24 dev+val snapshots, 849 release rows). Model-selection conclusion: on current data there is no evidence to adopt a form more complex than linear Q - lambda*P_hat. P_hat is decile-calibrated; within the compared range no nonlinear rule beat linear (this removes the miscalibration motivation for nonlinearity but not others: candidate-dependent loss, rotation-magnitude-dependent damage, nonlinear risk tolerance, coarse label proxy, score not being a utility). All families reached 0 selected topples (baseline only 3/24, so 3->0 and 0.005-level loss differences are unstable; family micro-ranking unreadable). Linear-lambda and hard-epsilon sweeps traced nearly the same empirical frontier on these snapshots/candidate sets/grids -- an observation, not a duality theorem (discrete candidate sets can have unsupported Pareto points). hard+fallback never starved offline, which does not rehabilitate the old static enforce gate nor rule out online starvation (live candidate generation differs). State-dependent lambda(s) untestable: remaining items spans 25-34 (scale 0.83-1.13) and is itself an unverified proxy for V_safe - V_fail; early snapshots would be added to identify whether failure loss varies with state.
entries.values: at 0 selected topples: hard eps=0.1 mean loss 0.042, quadratic 16 0.044, linear 2.0 0.047 (max loss 0.269 identical); at 1: quadratic 1.0 loss 0.007; top calibration decile predicted 0.713 vs observed 0.624

entries.claim: The official not_placed_safe judgment is close to a step function of settle angle: every band >= 45 deg is unconditionally unsafe (rate 1.000), 30-45 deg is mixed (0.375), and below 30 deg the rate is small (0.073) and displacement-driven (median 0.43 m among unsafe vs 0.06 m among safe). A smooth rotation-magnitude damage model therefore has little room -- one of the listed motivations for a nonlinear risk penalty is measured to be weak. rotated_over_30 is a slightly conservative but structurally faithful proxy for the angle channel; the residual loss mass below the threshold is the unresolved slide channel (d_xy). Exploratory scope: all non-holdout release rows (1121), not frozen-split metrics.

On the enlarged development+validation data (33 snapshots, 1180 release rows, 10 new near-terminal snapshots from 6 fresh trajectories) mechanics features still dominate static Phi for rotation, and the gap widened: LOSO AUC 0.819 [0.764, 0.870] vs static 0.698 [0.620, 0.767]; worst-direction extrapolation 0.697 vs 0.534; within-snapshot pair accuracy 0.824 vs 0.681 (n=7303). For not_placed_safe, static+mechanics is best (0.835 vs mech-only 0.809). Coefficients remain unfrozen pending validation-split selection.

Rule-family comparison replicated on 33 snapshots / 1180 release rows with baseline topples now 5/33: P_hat still decile-calibrated; every family reaches 0 selected topples, with matched-safety mean-loss differences within 0.004 of each other (at 0 rotated: quadratic-8 0.095, linear-2 0.098); state_scaled_linear still numerically identical to linear (remaining items 25-34, scale 0.838-1.140). Model-selection conclusion unchanged: no evidence to adopt a form more complex than linear Q - lambda*P_hat; the frontier costs rose because one new near-terminal snapshot has a large score spread (max loss 0.871 at zero-topple settings).

Live-stack shadow rerank at lambda=1.0 has now changed the selection on 4 of 33 dev/val snapshots (labelled pairs 4, unmatched 0): rotation danger difference 0 (1 vs 1), placed-safe difference +1 in shadow's favour, 0 safe->dangerous reversals, 1 dangerous->safe. Direction is favourable but the pair count is still far too small for the protocol's primary adoption metrics.

First online ablation (5 development configs, off vs live mechanics rerank at lambda 1/2/4, episode-level): every risk arm beat the submission-default baseline on aggregate placed (off 13.0 vs lam1 16.8 / lam2 14.0 / lam4 15.0) and fill (off 13.3 vs 17.1 / 16.7 / 17.4). Per-config: 4 of 5 configs improved or tied on placed under every lambda; fill improved even at equal placed (b000-k15: 14 placed both arms, fill 7.27 -> 15.39). Every episode still ends by an unsafe placement -- the risk term delays the topple, it does not eliminate it. Caveats: n=1 per (config, arm) at lambda 1/4; b000 episodes are deterministic under fixed timing while b001 episodes show timing nondeterminism with baseline variance up to 4 placed (b001-k20 off: 13 vs 17), so single-config differences of 1-3 are inconclusive there; the aggregate direction across configs and lambdas is the finding. Round 1 was invalidated by a stale simulator agent copy on both arms (instrument note in run_risk_ablation.py).

Confirmatory freeze per protocol 3.1/4: feature set = mechanics only (RELEASE_RISK_MECH_LOGISTIC_V1, mech-dev-v1-20260731, fit on development rows only), lambda = 1.0. Validation split (b000-k10, 74 rows, 2 snapshots) is near-ceiling for every feature set (AUC static 0.985 / mech 0.967 / static+mech 0.978 rotated) so it cannot discriminate; the choice rests on worst-direction extrapolation (mech 0.697 vs static 0.534) and online evidence. Online lambda selection on the unused validation case b000-k10: baseline is already near-optimal there (26 placed / 28.5 fill); lambda=1 ties placed, loses 1.2-1.8% fill, improves max settle angle 4->1 deg; lambda=2 clearly loses (24 placed, fill -22%) and is rejected; lambda=4 is mixed/nondeterministic. Combined with development configs (lambda=1 best aggregate placed 16.8 vs 13.3), lambda=1.0 is the only setting that never loses materially anywhere. Submission default stays risk-off until the one-shot final_holdout evaluation.

Official QA: unless a threshold number of items is loaded, every score component except fill becomes 0 (cutoff value undisclosed). Placed count is therefore a GATE for cog/stability/placement/soft scores, not just one metric among five -- episode survival (topple avoidance) matters more than any fill trade-off near the cutoff. Also: the composite total is a weighted aggregate of per-requirement evaluations with undisclosed weights/formulas.

Official QA: evaluation includes a shaking test; friction coefficients are stated to affect collapse risk at placement and shaking-test stability. stability_score is dynamic-response-based, raising the priority of the unresolved slide channel (d_xy) and Phi_slide item attributes (lateralFriction).
Official QA: items are cuboids with the centre of mass at the diagonal intersection (uniform density). The mechanics features' z_com = z_rest + h/2 assumption matches the official spec.

Official QA: inclusion_margin in the evaluation environment equals the bundled sample (-0.005); items placed flush against container walls are NOT counted toward fill. Wall-hugging placements lose fill credit -- affects candidate-generation wall margins.

One-shot final_holdout evaluation PASSED and the submission default switched to risk-on. Offline (frozen mech-dev-v1-20260731, no refit): rotated AUC 0.903 [0.761, 0.980], not_placed_safe 0.877 [0.684, 0.969] on 198 rows / 5 snapshots (per-case rotated: b001-k40 0.826, b001-k10 0.980; mech coefficients clean w.r.t. the noted provisional-v1 static contamination of b001-k40). Online (2 unseen cases x 2 repeats): placed mean off 16.25 -> lambda=1 18.0, fill 21.7 -> 22.6, catastrophic max settle angles (51-180 deg under off) reduced. agent.py defaults now RELEASE_RISK_LIVE_RERANK=1, RELEASE_RISK_P_MODEL=mech, lambda 1.0; env vars recover the old baseline. final_holdout is now OPENED: it can no longer serve as an unseen split, and future 'baseline' means the risk-on policy.

Slide direction is predictable from the pre-release contact state: on 422 release rows with |d_xy| > 5 cm, the mean cosine between the observed horizontal displacement and the CoM-offset-from-support-centroid direction is 0.651; 87.4% slide 'downhill' (cos > 0) and 76.3% have cos > 0.5. The long-unresolved d_xy channel was attacked with invariant scalars that discard direction; an equivariant formulation (predict in the local support frame, mirror symmetry by construction) is the indicated fix. Ladder: S0 equivariant baseline without new losses -> S1 learned local-geometry encoder with invariance loss -> S2 test fixed SketchGeo vs Gated Iota on the frozen worst-group extrapolation metrics (user's loss-function document, 2026-07-31).
entries.source: inline probe over 33-snapshot dev+val replay rows; docs/theory (pending S0 script)

entries.claim: The d_xy channel yields to the equivariant local-frame formulation (S0, no learned representation): LOSO Spearman |d_xy| 0.282 -> 0.567, signed longitudinal 0.641, large-slide AUC 0.718 -> 0.787, and worst-side extrapolation 0.037 -> 0.399 (better on 6 of 7 sides; only the easy k10 side favours the invariant baseline). Mirror-symmetry prediction confirmed label-side: mean |transverse| 0.039 m vs |longitudinal| 0.085 m. Direction is carried by the zero-parameter downhill prior (0.856); the model's contribution is magnitude and extrapolation stability. Features: com_offset, downhill/uphill margins to the support hull, mechanics scalars, friction/mass/density/is_soft. S1 (learned local-geometry encoder + invariance loss) and S2 (SketchGeo vs Gated Iota on worst-group metrics) remain open as the next rungs.

Post-mortem of 57 episode-ending placements (all ablation episodes; container rebuilt from observed settle AABBs, frozen mech P_rot on the commanded pose): death channels are topple 28, transport_invalid 21, slide 8. Within topples the rotation model mostly saw it coming -- KNOWN (P_rot>=0.5) 6, AMBIGUOUS (0.2-0.5) 17, MISSED (<0.2) only 5 -- so the topple-channel remainder is starvation / insufficient endgame penalty (a state-dependent lambda argument), not perception. The largest untapped lever is the transport_invalid channel (37% of deaths, untouchable by any release-risk lambda): episodes die on transport validation before physics, pointing back at candidate generation / anchor recall in endgame states.

First slide online ablation (5 dev configs, base vs slide lambda 0.5 / 1.0 on top of rot-only lambda=1): slide lambda trades placed for slide-death reduction -- lambda=1.0 cut low-angle unsafe endings 4 -> 1 but cost 4.4 placed per episode (18.4 -> 14.0); lambda=0.5 gained fill (+2.0) at -1.8 placed with slide deaths unchanged. Under the official cutoff gate (placed count gates all non-fill scores) this trade is rejected: RELEASE_RISK_SLIDE_LAMBDA stays 0 in the live default. Slide shadow produced zero changed single selections (4 steps) -- the slide term acts through cumulative trajectory divergence, not single-step swaps. The frozen slide model (slide-dev-v1-20260731) remains available; revisit after S1 improves the estimator or with smaller lambda once the transport channel is fixed.

Candidate supply is NOT the endgame constraint: at all 27 late replay snapshots (steps 11-16, dev+val), the HT-estimated population of official-transport-valid candidates is in the thousands (minimum ~1038, typically 10k-36k), physically placeable-safe candidates are also in the thousands (never zero), and the minimum frozen-mech P_rot among valid sampled candidates is 0.003-0.101. Per the terminal-failure trichotomy: transport_invalid deaths (21) mean the anytime search failed to find/execute any of thousands of valid candidates within budget (recall failure, plausibly the 8 s timeout -> forced random action), and topple deaths mean risky candidates were chosen while near-zero-risk options existed (selection/recall, not perception, and not candidate starvation). Caveat: measured on replay snapshots near-terminal, not the exact dying states of the ablation episodes.
entries.source: inline probe over 33-snapshot replay data (population counts + is_valid/is_placed_safe HT weights + frozen mech P_rot); consistent with anchor-recall-one-snapshot (0.167)

entries.claim: The packed-AABB cache (6.4x candidate throughput) produced a MIXED regression-guard result: b000-k40 +10 placed (11->21, fill 14->27 -- search starvation was binding there) and b000-k15 +1, but b000-k20 -12 (26->14) and b001-k20 -6; net placed 92->84 across the 5 dev configs. Interpretation: higher recall changes every selection, and with the known-defective utility (Ranker volume dead vote, q+gamma*q lookahead) a larger candidate pool can select worse trajectories -- the starved search was acting as an accidental regularizer. The cache is kept (the 78%-waste defect is real and the starvation mechanism is not a defensible control), which promotes selection quality under enlarged candidate sets (Ranker/lookahead) from deferred to blocking. Guard episodes are single trajectories; b001 configs carry timing nondeterminism, but the b000-k20 drop is deterministic-environment real.
entries.source: reports/benchmarks/baseline.json vs base-r7 guard episodes; commit of the cache change
